identity.title: ALMA CO Observations of the Host Galaxies of Long-duration Gamma-Ray Bursts. I. Molecular Gas Scaling Relations

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present the results of CO observations toward 14 host galaxies of long-duration gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) at $z = 0.1$–2.5 by using the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array.

distance_source.value: Spectroscopic redshifts from the literature (Table 1 references); luminosity distance from H0=70, Om=0.3, OL=0.7

question.value: Do GRB host galaxies have molecular gas properties (gas fraction, depletion time) that differ from other star-forming galaxies, once selection bias relative to the main sequence is accounted for?

evidence.quote: In order to understand the molecular gas properties in GRB hosts, a larger sample with CO observations is necessary.

analysis_steps.goal: Measure CO line fluxes and continuum

method.value: Velocity-integrated CO maps and continuum maps; 3 sigma upper limits for non-detections assuming 180 km/s line width

evidence.quote: For non-detection hosts, we derived 3$\sigma$ upper limits by assuming a line width of 180 km s$^{-1}$

analysis_steps.goal: SED fitting for SFR and stellar mass

method.value: CIGALE with delayed SFH, BC03 SSP, Chabrier IMF, nebular emission, modified starburst attenuation, dl2014 dust emission, radio module

evidence.quote: We adopt a SFH of the delayed SFH with an optional exponential burst (`sfhdelayed`)
The models are fitted to the data and physical properties are estimated through the analysis of the likelihood distribution.

validation.value: Stellar masses compared with previous studies

method.value: L'CO from Solomon & Vanden Bout formula, converted to CO(1–0) with r31=0.6, r41=0.4, times metallicity-dependent alpha_CO

evidence.quote: we adopted the line ratios of CO(3–2)/CO(1–0) $=r_{31}$ $=0.6$ and CO(4–3)/CO(1–0) $=r_{41}$ $=0.4$

assumptions.value: alpha_CO(Z) of Genzel+15 (harmonic mean of Genzel+12 and Bolatto+13 at low metallicity), metallicity on Pettini & Pagel scale

claims.hypothesis: GRB hosts have higher gas fraction and shorter depletion time than other SFGs
claims.experiment: Compare mu_gas and t_depl vs redshift with Tacconi+18 sample
claims.result: GRB hosts tend to have higher mu_gas and shorter t_depl, especially z<~1
claims.finding: Could be a common property or selection effect from being above the MS

evidence.loc: 5.3 Gas Fraction, Depletion Timescale, and Scaling Relation
evidence.quote: The GRB hosts tend to have a higher $\mu_{\rm gas}$ and a shorter $t_{\rm depl}$ as compared with other star-forming galaxies at similar redshifts

claims.hypothesis: GRB hosts follow the same δMS scaling relations as other SFGs
claims.result: mu_gas increases and t_depl decreases with δMS; r=0.79, -0.59
claims.finding: No molecular gas deficit at given SFR and stellar mass

evidence.loc: 5.3 Gas Fraction, Depletion Timescale, and Scaling Relation
evidence.quote: The GRB hosts follow the same scaling trends as other star-forming galaxies, where $\mu_{\rm gas}$ increases and $t_{\rm depl}$ decreases with increasing $\delta {\rm MS}$.

claims.hypothesis: GRB hosts share dynamics with other SFGs
claims.result: Hosts overlap MS and local galaxies

evidence.quote: the GRB hosts appear to follow the model relation, which is also applied to $z \sim 1$–2 MS galaxies
